title: Metric life-cycle checklist for feature gating
body:
Purpose:
This is a practical, checklist-style note for instrumenting, validating, and retiring metrics that are used to gate feature rollouts. The goal is to avoid metric sprawl, control cardinality/cost, and ensure that the gating signal is reliable and debuggable with traces and compact dashboards. This doc is intentionally operational and short-form — use it when planning new feature gates or reviewing existing ones.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focus is on feature rollouts that depend on telemetry (percent-traffic gating, dark launches, A/B toggles) for automated decisioning or human-run rollouts.
- Applies to both hosted and dedicated deployments where telemetry semantics are shared.
- We assume existing baseline infra: metrics pipeline (prom/OTel -> metrics store), traces (OTel -> tracing backend), and dashboard platform.

Checklist (before enabling a gating metric in prod):
1) Define the metric and owner
   - metric_name (proto): feature.gate.<feature_id>.decision_count
   - flavor: counter (increment per decision), with labels: outcome, region, model_variant, route
   - owner: product-engineer or eng-sre oncall (explicit)
   - doc: short description, expected cardinality, and a reference to the gating RFC

2) Evaluate cardinality and labels
   - list required labels and estimate cardinality per-hour. Aim for <= 10k series across all shards for high-volume gates.
   - prefer low-cardinality labels (region, outcome, variant). Avoid user_id/session_id as a label — use tracing to join to identity when needed.
   - if identifying cohorts necessary, plan a hashed_cohort label with bounded buckets (e.g., hashed_cohort=mod100).

3) Sampling and aggregation plan
   - decide sampling at ingestion if expected QPS is high (sample decisions at 1% with reservoir sampling for tail analysis).
   - provide a derived aggregated metric for low-cardinality dashboards: feature.gate.<feature_id>.decision_rate (per-route 1m-rate).
   - document how sampled traces will be correlated (trace id in logs, sampling keys).

4) Trace anchors and instrumentation hooks
   - instrument the decision path with a short-span named gate.decision that includes attributes: gate_id, input_hash, decision_outcome, model_variant, latency_ms.
   - ensure span is emitted even for quick-pass decisions (should be sub-ms but still present) so we can chain to downstream inference spans.
   - add an event in the parent request span with the gate decision and minimal payload to avoid high cardinality.

5) Dashboard and alert design
   - dashboard sprint: create a compact 3-panel widget set per feature gate: (1) decision_rate (1m p50/p95), (2) outcome_breakdown (stacked bar), (3) decision_latency_histogram.
   - include a topline KPI widget: % of traffic gated (calc: gated_count / total_request_count).
   - add an investigation link (trace search query) that filters traces with span gate.decision and decision_outcome!=expected.
   - alerting: create two alerts — (A) sustained change in decision distribution (>5% delta vs baseline for 15m), (B) spike in decision latency (p95 above threshold for 10m). Keep alerts aggregated by team, not by fine-grained label.

6) Cost and retention guardrails
   - set metric retention for raw series used by gating to 30d; aggregated rollups kept 90d if used for business metrics.
   - add quota tags to metric writes: product=feature-gating, cost_center=… so billing and quotas can be applied.
   - enforce label whitelists via instrumentation linter in the SDK to prevent accidental high-cardinality labels.

7) Ownership, runbook, and rollback signal
   - assign an oncall owner for the first 48–72 hours after rollout. Owner responsibilities: watch dashboards, respond to alerts, examine traces for anomalies.
   - define rollback criteria in the rollout RFC: example triggers — >3% user-visible error increase, >10% p95 latency regressions lasting >30m, or poor decision distribution.
   - include an automated rollback hook if metric health degrades beyond defined thresholds (infra team integration).

8) Validation and canary checks
   - run a canary with 1% traffic for 24–72 hours. Validate metric stability: series count, zero-flapping of labels, sample trace availability.
   - run synthetic tests that force each decision_outcome at least N times to validate downstream dashboards and alerts (N=50).

9) Post-rollout hygiene
   - schedule a reviews ticket at 30d to evaluate metric usage. If the metric is not on any dashboard or used in alerts, consider retiring.
   - if retiring, plan: (a) mark metric deprecated in docs, (b) remove from dashboards, (c) set a retention taper to 7d then delete after 90d deprecation window.

Instrumentation examples (examples to paste into code):
- Metrics SDK (pseudo):
  metrics.counter("feature.gate.checkout_v2.decision_count", labels={"outcome": outcome, "variant": variant, "region": region}).inc()
- Trace span (pseudo):
  with tracer.start_span("gate.decision", attributes={"gate_id":"checkout_v2","variant":variant,"outcome":outcome}) as s:
      s.set_attribute("decision_latency_ms", latency_ms)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we model a canonical derived metric pattern for all gates (decision_rate + decision_latency) and enforce that via templates? (action: product + observability)
- For high-cardinality cohorting needs, do we leverage metrics or move to ad-hoc log/tracing queries? Need cost comparison (action: infra-costs).
- Automation for retirement: can we add a dashboard usage exporter to flag unused metrics automatically? (action: observability team exploration)

Quick-links for oncall investigation (copy-paste):
- Trace query: service="api" AND span:"gate.decision" AND attribute.gate_id:"{feature}" AND attribute.decision_outcome:unexpected
- Dashboard: Observability / Feature Gates / {feature_id} (placeholder)
- Runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/gating-runbook

Appendix: small rubric for deciding label inclusion
- Include label if: it's necessary to route decisions (region/model_variant), needed for automated rollbacks, or required by compliance.
- Exclude label if: it can be derived from a trace, it is user-identifying, or its cardinality will blow up (>100 distinct values/hour).

Notes to self (short):
- Keep dashboards small and investigation-forward. 3 panels + trace link is usually enough.
- Prioritize low-cardinality aggregates and rely on traces for deep dives.
- Linter + CI enforcement for metric labels will reduce accidental spikes in series count.

If you plan to use this for a real rollout, ping me (Sofia) or drop details in #observability and we’ll do a quick 15m review before you flip the gate.
